mechanistic_link: Human engineered graft -> IL10 transcript evidence
key_evidence: Probe/molecule-level reconstruction reproduced canonical IL10 counts in Tx17 (18 UMI / 13 cells) and Tx5 (4 UMI / 4 cells). SfLB1 had 2 singleton MEX events and SfLB2 had 0; stringent all-four shared-TRUE probe sensitivity was SfLB1=0, SfLB2=0, Tx17=5, Tx5=0.
direction_result: IL10 transcript signal is reproducibly present in both Tx graft samples; stringent shared-probe sensitivity retains Tx17 signal.
replicate_consistency: Tx17 and Tx5 both positive in canonical gene-level/molecule reconstruction; strict shared-probe sensitivity is Tx17-positive / Tx5-zero.
strength: High for transcript detection; Moderate for transgene-specific attribution
causal_boundary: Gene-level IL10 cannot by itself distinguish endogenous from transgene-derived transcript; transcript detection does not demonstrate secreted IL10 protein.
paper_safe_wording: IL10 was detected in both Tx graft samples in the standard filtered gene-expression matrix and reproduced at molecule/probe level. A stringent shared-probe sensitivity analysis retained signal in Tx17 but not Tx5.

mechanistic_link: Human graft ligands -> mouse host receiver landscape
biological_unit: Mouse host broad liver lineages, sample-level descriptive summaries
key_evidence: IL10R dual-positive competence was concentrated in myeloid lineages relevant to the treatment mechanism; Tx mean dual-positive fractions were ~34.4% in Kupffer/Macrophage and ~25.2% in Monocyte. Other ligand-receptor bridges showed lineage-specific patterns (e.g., VEGFA->LSEC; FGF1/TNFSF12/HBEGF/BTC->hepatobiliary/HSC compartments).
direction_result: Mouse host myeloid cells are a major receptor-competent compartment for the engineered IL10 anchor.
replicate_consistency: Receiver competence retained in both Tx17 and Tx5; descriptive n=2 Sham vs n=2 Tx.
causal_boundary: Receptor transcript co-detection/competence is not ligand binding, receptor occupancy, JAK activation, or pSTAT3.
paper_safe_wording: Mouse host macrophage/monocyte compartments retain substantial Il10ra/Il10rb receptor-transcript competence after transplantation.

biological_unit: Final Clean-B mouse MΦ states; Sham1/Sham20 vs Tx17/Tx5
key_evidence: MΦ composition shifted in a treatment-consistent direction: Inflammatory-MΦ ~27.0%->18.1%; Anti-inflammatory-MΦ ~28.9%->33.4%; ECM-associated inflammatory-MΦ ~9.0%->7.9%; Repair/Resolution-MΦ ~2.8%->5.3%. IL10R dual-positive fraction increased across all five MΦ classes.
direction_result: Tx is associated with reduced inflammatory/profibrotic MΦ abundance and increased anti-inflammatory/repair-associated MΦ abundance.
replicate_consistency: Direction was concordant across Tx17 and Tx5 for the principal composition changes.
causal_boundary: This is comparative single-cell association. The all-MΦ IL10_STAT3 and downstream-no-receptor programs were not increased (approximately -0.746 and -0.610 respectively), so canonical IL10->STAT3 transcriptional activation is not directly demonstrated.
paper_safe_wording: Transplantation was associated with macrophage-state remodeling away from inflammatory/ECM-associated inflammatory states and toward anti-inflammatory and repair/resolution states, while transcript-level evidence of sustained canonical IL10-STAT3 activation was not observed.

biological_unit: Repair/Resolution-MΦ, within-sample IL10R dual-positive vs not-dual-positive
key_evidence: C2.1 IL10R fractions reproduced exactly. v6.3.6 Repair/Resolution-MΦ Pdgfb benchmark was reproduced (Sham 5.970686 vs checkpoint 5.971 CP10k; Tx 3.568014 vs checkpoint 3.568). Within Tx, mean per-cell Pdgfb was lower in IL10R-dual-positive cells in Tx17 (-2.543 CP10k) and Tx5 (-0.034), but pseudobulk contrast was Tx17 -2.214 and Tx5 +0.060; Sham also showed negative per-cell contrasts.
direction_result: No Tx-specific, replicate-consistent direct IL10R-status -> Pdgfb suppression bridge.
replicate_consistency: Not sufficient across metrics; Tx5 pseudobulk direction differs and Sham shows a similar inverse association.
causal_boundary: Do not claim cell-autonomous IL10R activation directly suppresses Pdgfb from this scRNA-seq dataset.
paper_safe_wording: IL10R transcript status did not provide a Tx-specific, replicate-consistent cell-autonomous explanation for Pdgfb suppression; IL10-responsive macrophage remodeling and PDGF attenuation are therefore linked at the network/treatment-phenotype level rather than by a directly demonstrated intracellular chain.

biological_unit: Repair/Resolution-MΦ sender and ECM-activated HSC receiver; Sham1/Sham20 vs Tx17/Tx5
key_evidence: Repair/Resolution-MΦ Pdgfb per-cell: 5.971->3.568 CP10k. CellChat PDGF communication Repair/Resolution-MΦ -> ECM-activated HSC: ~0.1846->~0.1088. ECM-HSC PDGF mitogenic module: ~+0.479->~-0.479.
direction_result: Selective attenuation of a PDGF-associated mitogenic/proliferative MΦ-to-HSC signaling arm.
replicate_consistency: Checkpoint classified the axis as strong/coherent Tx-down evidence with biological-sample-aware analyses.
causal_boundary: Not global HSC suppression. FN1 communication increased in Tx, demonstrating pathway-selective rewiring rather than uniform suppression.
paper_safe_wording: The macrophage-HSC interaction analysis supports selective attenuation of a PDGF-associated mitogenic/proliferative signaling arm after transplantation, rather than global suppression of HSC biology.

mechanistic_link: PDGF attenuation -> reduced activated/cycling HSC burden
key_evidence: ECM-activated HSC fraction ~0.527->~0.452; cycling fraction within ECM-activated HSC ~0.0560->~0.0478; cycling ECM-HSC burden within HSC3 ~0.0298->~0.0216.
direction_result: Activated/proliferative HSC burden decreases after Tx, consistent with reduced fibrogenic drive.
replicate_consistency: Strong-to-moderate Tx-down evidence in v6.3.6 checkpoint.
causal_boundary: Association is mechanistically coherent with PDGF attenuation but does not by itself prove PDGF is the sole cause of fibrosis improvement.
paper_safe_wording: Transplantation reduced ECM-activated and cycling HSC burden in parallel with attenuation of the macrophage-to-HSC PDGF mitogenic axis.

mechanistic_link: Mouse-defined IL10-responsive myeloid architecture -> human MASH target conservation
biological_unit: Human LT1-LT8 final myeloid states; single-cell RNA counts and state-level pseudobulk
key_evidence: All five final human myeloid states retained IL10RA and IL10RB at state level. In advanced LT1/LT2 (NAS6/F4-F3), same-cell IL10RA+IL10RB dual-positive fractions in PRIMARY states were Resident/Kupffer-like 24.7%, Repair/Resolution 28.3%, and Inflammatory/Transitional 17.9% (LT1/LT2 mean). Both advanced samples contained dual-positive cells in all three PRIMARY states.
direction_result: Advanced human MASH retains a receptor-transcript-competent myeloid target compartment corresponding to the mouse IL10-responsive architecture.
replicate_consistency: Same-cell dual-positive cells detected in both LT1 and LT2 for all three PRIMARY states.
causal_boundary: Does not show IL10 treatment response in humans; transcript co-detection is not receptor protein, ligand exposure, or pSTAT3. Advanced NAS6 samples are also F3/F4, so disease-severity effects are confounded with fibrosis.
paper_safe_wording: Advanced human MASH retains same-cell IL10RA/IL10RB transcript co-detection across major myeloid states, supporting the biological availability of an IL10-responsive myeloid target compartment in human disease.

key_evidence: Human graft IL10 transcript evidence; mouse host myeloid IL10R competence; Tx-associated macrophage-state remodeling; selective MΦ-to-ECM-HSC PDGF attenuation; reduced activated/cycling HSC burden; advanced human MASH retains same-cell IL10RA/IL10RB-positive myeloid targets.
direction_result: Network-level closure supports: engineered graft IL10 / graft secretome -> receptor-competent host myeloid compartment -> macrophage remodeling and selective PDGF-axis rewiring -> reduced fibrogenic HSC activity -> fibrosis improvement; the corresponding IL10-responsive target architecture is retained in human MASH.
replicate_consistency: Major mouse and human links are replicate-aware; direct IL10R->Pdgfb intracellular linkage is the explicit non-closed link.
strength: High at network level; not a fully causal intracellular chain
causal_boundary: Do not state that scRNA-seq proves IL10 protein secretion, pSTAT3 activation, or direct IL10R-mediated repression of Pdgfb. The supported model is pathway/network-level convergence.
paper_safe_wording: Together, the data support a cross-species model in which the engineered graft engages a receptor-competent host myeloid compartment, is associated with macrophage-state remodeling and selective attenuation of macrophage-to-HSC PDGF signaling, and thereby converges on reduced fibrogenic HSC activity. Human MASH retains the corresponding IL10 receptor-transcript-competent myeloid target compartment.
